supported_scope: Detection of the nine planted defect classes in tests/fixtures/benchmarks, measured at recall 1.0 against a baseline of 0.125.
Reproducibility: the fact sets are byte-identical across runs of an unchanged tree.
Structural depth on Python and on Go, measured on two real repositories: 97.3% of Python imports and 97.7% of non-Python imports resolve, and 95.4% of the eight load questions are answered.
Every claim carries evidence and a falsifier, every document stays inside a declared line budget, and every declared invariant has a test enforcing it: 71 of 71.
The four pinned engines are exercised during measurement, and a report produced without them is refused rather than scored.
unsupported_scope: Any claim about unseen repositories: the two measured cases are this tool and one Go project it was tuned against.
Usefulness to a reader: no independent person has judged a claim or a card.
Whether the transformation plan's predictions come true: nothing has executed a stage and measured the result.
The semantic arm: no model provider ran, so nothing is known about interpretation quality.
Comparison against a plain agent: never performed.
Languages beyond Python and Go: parsed, but detection depth is unmeasured.
Repositories above a few thousand files: performance and precision at that size are unmeasured.
limits: This record exists to stop a pilot being described as a release. Seven of nine capability domains are at target and the two that are not cannot be closed by a model: one needs a stage actually executed, the other needs a human reviewer. It supports a pilot only.

not_at_target.transformation_plan: scores 1.0 on its three measurable indicators; predictions_verified is unmeasured because a guarantee needs a report taken after the change, and the engine never writes code
not_at_target.independent_proof: 0.0 until a reviewer outside this project completes evaluations/review-pack; no model can close it
